 Nashville Predators defenseman Adam Wilsby, right, and Boston Bruins center James Hagens battle for the puck as the Bruins take on the Predators. Stuart Cahill/Boston Herald 
 By Steve Conroy | sconroy@bostonherald.com | Boston Herald PUBLISHED: October 24, 2026 at 1:14 PM EDT | UPDATED: October 24, 2026 at 2:43 PM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... There was understandably a lot of excitement surrounding the arrival of James Hagens. Not only was he the seventh overall draft pick in 2025, fans around here saw the highly-skilled forward on a regular basis at Boston College the last two seasons.
 But no one expected him to be leading all NHL forwards in one particularly category – blocked shots.
 Going into Saturday’s NHL games, the 19-year-old Hagens had 16 blocks, including three in Thursday’s win over the Nashville Predators.
 “I don’t think that was on my bingo card at all,” said Hagens with a laugh. “But when it’s your turn, you’ve got to be ready and willing to get in front of it.”
 It’s early in the season, but the stat has caught the eye of a lot of his older teammates.
 “That’s a surprising one for a lot of us, I think,” Hagens’ linemate Casey Mittelstadt said. “Obviously kudos to him. He’s getting in the way. In the last game, I think he had three on (Roman) Josi alone, which is not an easy one to block. Impressive, for sure.”
 While younger players are having more and more of an impact in today’s NHL, Hagens has embraced his ongoing education in the game, including the less glamorous parts. A natural centerman, he’s been playing on the wing this season. And while he’s been a big point producer at every level at which he’s played, Hagens has been on what has essentially been a checking line with Mittelstadt and Elias Lindholm.
 “Every day, whether it’s another practice or a game, you can always learn,” Hagens said. “For me, it’s just being able to go out there, talk with my linemates and the guys on the team, also being able to learn from the other guys what they’re doing. The coaches are talking, making sure you’re listening, so that’s been something that’s been really helpful for me.”
 He’s also enjoying the challenge of facing some of the top players in the league.
 “It’s crazy to be able to go out there against some of the best players in the world. It’s an honor,” Hagens said. “But at the same time, you really have to be able to take responsibility in defense and try to generate offense when you get the chance.”
